Eagle Scout service project

A shed and accessible sink for Animal Assisted Happiness

For my Eagle Scout project, I planned, budgeted, and led the construction of a shed structure and an accessible sink at Animal Assisted Happiness. I organized the workdays and taught volunteers how to carry out tasks safely. Other Scouts, adult volunteers, and the beneficiary helped complete the work.

01 / Overview

Project Overview

The farm needed a place for a washer and dryer to clean animal bedding, along with a handwashing location that people with disabilities could use. My project included a shed with a floor, roof, and framing for two walls, as well as replacing an old sink and countertop.

I developed the drawings, researched materials and accessibility requirements, planned the budget, and led the construction workdays. A volunteer at the farm also gave me advice during planning.

02 / Planning

Planning & Design Changes

The original proposal was an open shedrow with four posts and a roof. As the beneficiary’s needs changed from storage to a laundry room, the project expanded to include a floor and wall framing. This required changes to most of my plans, including the material lists, cost estimates, time estimates, and tasks for each workday.

We agreed that my team would build the structure and the beneficiary would finish the walls and remaining enclosure work. During planning, I also incorporated advice to use redwood and post-base brackets to improve resistance to rot.

03 / Construction

Construction

I divided the construction into stages so volunteers knew what needed to happen each day. These included marking the post locations, digging holes, setting and leveling the brackets, pouring concrete, installing posts and beams, and adding rafters and roofing. The expanded project also included the floor and wall framing.

For the sink, the work included removing the old fixture, cutting openings in the countertop, adding support for the new sink, and connecting the plumbing. I explained the tasks and safety precautions before work began. My safety plan assigned cutting tasks to adults.

04 / Leadership

Leadership & Challenges

At the beginning, I found it difficult to step back and let other people do the work. I also struggled to organize multiple tasks at the same time. As the project progressed, I adjusted which volunteers attended each day based on the jobs available and organized more tasks to happen at once. This gave people more useful work to do.

I also put off parts of the planning. During construction, several tasks took longer than expected, so we stayed later than planned to finish within the expected number of workdays.

We ran short of some nails and screws, but had enough to finish each day’s work. I bought more supplies before the next workday and returned excess wood at the end of the project.

05 / Results

Results & Lessons Learned

We completed the structural work and sink installation within the available funds and without injuries. The beneficiary completed the shed’s enclosure after my team’s structural work.

The main lessons for me were to plan further ahead and organize work so several tasks could happen at once. By the end of the project, I was better at keeping volunteers involved and allowing them to carry out the work themselves. Planning which people and tasks were needed for each day helped me lead the later workdays more effectively.
